summary: Relevance-gated primary floor: pull relevant primary root texts into top-15 so synthesis works don't crowd them out — NO synthesis score penalty
description: Follow-through from the §8.1 calibration finding (todo:19ea34ea, docs/retrieval-golden-gap-investigation.md): both vector-score levers (length-norm, hub-dampen) REGRESSED and were reverted. Root cause — the fluency inversion is a primary-vs-synthesis distinction, not era, and a global score penalty is the wrong instrument (it buries synthesis's genuine insight everywhere). CORRECT instrument: a slot-level PROMOTION — when a query has a relevant primary root text being crowded out, reserve it a top-15 slot; synthesis scores are untouched, so on a mixed query the reader gets primary AND synthesis both. Baseline to hold: 314/6 (cap-off default). Scope note: this addresses the crowding/scoring failures (poetic-edda, paracelsus, iamblichus, mabinogion, and pistis — whose crowders are other-tradition primaries, so a per-tradition floor lifts it); it does NOT address isa-upanishad, which never enters the candidate pool (that is §8.3 recall, out of scope here). Work the children in order; c2/c3 are gated on c1 showing a clean recovery.
